newsitem.title: USA: Procter & Gamble sales cut by currencies.
newsitem.headline: Procter & Gamble sales cut by currencies.

text.p: Procter & Gamble Co said on Thursday that worldwide unit volume growth rose four percent for the third quarter but sales were up two percent, a difference the company attributed to unfavorable currency translation.
P&G reported net income per share of $1.18 on a diluted basis ($1.26 primary), compared to $1.01 for the same period a year ago. The First Call Q3 estimate was $1.23.

North American unit volume was up two percent for the quarter but sales were stable, reflecting in part lower pricing in the laundry category. Net earnings rose six percent, helped by greater cost savings, P&G said.
Unit volume for Europe, the Middle East and Africa was up nine percent for the quarter but sales rose only three percent, held back by unfavorable exchange rates. Net earnings rose 20 percent.
For Asia, unit volume declined one percent, due in part to competitive pressure in Japan. Sales for the region were up one percent, led by China, and net earnings rose 37 percent.
Unit volume in Latin America rose one percent, sales grew 12 percent and net earnings rose 53 percent, the company said.
